paper.title_en: Role of crystal-field degrees of freedom in square and rectangular skyrmion lattices in noncentrosymmetric tetragonal magnets
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the role of crystal-field degrees of freedom in stabilizing square and rectangular skyrmion lattices in a noncentrosymmetric localized-moment model on a square lattice. The magnetic phases are determined using self-consistent mean-field calculations. We first consider a single crystal-field doublet with exchange and polar-type Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions. We find square skyrmion lattices with distinct magnetic periods, as well as a rectangular skyrmion lattice that spontaneously breaks the in-plane fourfold rotational symmetry. Their stability and field-induced phase sequences are strongly controlled by the crystal-field wave function, including reentrant behavior of the rectangular phase. Second-neighbor exchange further modifies the competition among these states. When a second crystal-field doublet is retained, additional rectangular skyrmion lattices with distinct modulation patterns emerge, together with axial single-$Q$ states and various double-$Q$ states. These results demonstrate that crystal-field degrees of freedom provide a microscopic mechanism for tuning the stability, spatial symmetry, and topology of multiple-$Q$ magnetic states.
